body: ## Confirm before you write
- Before issuing a credit note or opening a dispute, tell the customer exactly what you are about to do: the invoice line, and for a credit the amount. Ask them to confirm. Write only after the customer explicitly says yes in the conversation.
- If the customer says no, or doesn't answer, write nothing for it: no credit note, no dispute, no case. Tell them nothing has been changed and that they can come back to Support if they change their mind.
- This applies to every credit and dispute, whatever the amount. Escalating a case without a dispute doesn't need this confirmation.

## No early promises
- Don't tell a customer a credit is likely or coming before the console confirms it's a duplicate.

## Why
In the 2026 quality review, most complaints about credits weren't about the amount: customers hadn't known a write was about to happen, or had been told a credit was coming before the console confirmed anything. These standards fix both.

## Saying what you're about to do
Name the action, the invoice line and, for a credit, the amount. For example: "I'll issue a credit note for the duplicated line L2 on invoice INV-…, for the full amount of that line. Shall I go ahead?"

## What counts as a yes
- A clear yes to the action you described: "yes", "go ahead", "please do".
- Not a yes: a question, "maybe", "I guess", a yes to something else, or silence.
- If the customer changes the request after you asked, describe the new action and ask again.

## Handoffs
Escalating a case to another team without a credit note or dispute doesn't need this confirmation. Tell the customer which team has it.

## Tone
- Plain language, no internal team or tool names the customer can't use.
- One answer per question, in the order they asked.
- Don't apologise for policy; explain it.

## Measuring it
Support QA samples 5% of conversations each week and scores confirmation, accuracy and tone. Results are shared in the monthly support review.

##### security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/payment-card-data-handling-standard-2027.json
title: Payment Card Data Handling Standard (2027)
status: published
last_updated: 2027-04-02
body: ## Purpose
Redwood never handles payment card numbers itself: cards are entered by customers in Console billing settings, which hands them straight to the payment processor. This standard keeps card numbers out of every Redwood system that isn't the processor's, so that Redwood stays outside PCI DSS cardholder-data scope. It is owned by Security and applies from 26 March 2027.

## Scope
- Every Redwood employee and contractor, and every automated agent acting for Redwood, including the support agent.
- Every channel a customer can write or speak in: chat, email, the support portal and, from 1 April 2027, the voice channel.
- Every place text is kept: replies, cases, disputes, notes, transcripts, tickets, Slack and documents.

## The rule
Never repeat, store or forward a payment card number, in any form. That covers plain digits, digits with spaces or dashes, partial numbers including the last four digits, and digits spoken or written out as words. Voice transcripts write spoken digits as words, so "four one one one" is a card number too.

## What Support does
- If a customer shares a card number, don't repeat it or any part of it. Tell them not to send card details to Support.
- Support doesn't change payment methods and doesn't take card numbers for any reason. A customer changes the card used for autopay themselves, in Console billing settings.
- A request to change a card needs no case. Point the customer to Console billing settings.
- If you need to mention it in a case for another reason, write "customer shared a card number (removed)". Never the number or any part of it.
- Sharing a card doesn't change how a billing problem is routed: a payment failure is handled as the billing case routing page describes.

## Detection and redaction
- The support tooling scans incoming messages and transcripts for card-number patterns and masks them before they are stored. Masking is a safety net, not permission: the rule above still applies to what an agent writes.
- The weekly data-loss-prevention scan covers cases, disputes, notes and Slack. Matches are reviewed by Security within two business days.
- An unmasked card number found anywhere is handled by Security as a data-handling incident: the text is purged and the owner of the system is told. Support doesn't open a billing case for it.

## Other teams
- **Sales and account teams**: never ask for card details on calls or in email; enterprise customers paying by invoice don't need a card on file.
- **Billing Ops**: works from processor references (payment IDs and decline codes), never card numbers.
- **Engineering**: logs must not capture request bodies from the billing settings page. Test cards are used in staging only.

## Training and evidence
- New support staff complete the card-data module before their first shift; everyone repeats it yearly.
- Security keeps the training records, the DLP scan reports and the data-handling incident log as evidence for the annual compliance review.

## Exceptions
None. A customer's request, a manager's approval or an urgent payment doesn't make an exception to this standard.

## Contacts
Security: Kevin Osei. Questions in #security.

title: Collections: Dunning Schedule for Overdue Invoices (2027)
status: published

body: ## Scope
Invoices still unpaid after their due date, once any automatic payment retries have finished. Payments that fail during a payment-processor incident are retried automatically and are not overdue; this page doesn't apply to them.

|---|---|

body: ## Pricing
Batch API jobs are billed at 50% of the Hosted API per-token rate for the same model, with a completion window of 24 hours.

## How it shows on an invoice
Batch usage is billed on its own invoice lines, one per week, described as "Batch jobs, <start>-<end>". Each line links to the jobs it bills.

## Limits
- Up to 50,000 requests per job.
- Jobs that don't finish in 24 hours are cancelled; finished requests in a cancelled job are billed, unfinished ones are not.

title: Known issue: Embeddings Batch usage can take up to 4 hours to appear
status: published
last_updated: 2027-03-12
body: ## Scope
This applies only to the Embeddings Batch endpoint (`/v1/embeddings/batch`). Its usage is written when the whole batch finishes, so it can take up to 4 hours to appear on the Console usage page. It does not apply to Hosted API requests or ordinary embeddings calls; for those, the threshold is on the billing case routing page.

## What to tell the customer
Batch usage appears when the batch finishes. No case is needed within 4 hours of the batch finishing.

##### customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/console-invoice-list-sort-order-2027.json
title: Known issue: Console invoice list sorts by issue date
status: published
last_updated: 2027-03-05
body: ## Symptom
The Console invoice list sorts by the date an invoice was issued, not the period it covers, so a re-issued invoice for an earlier month can appear at the top.

## Workaround
Use the period filter or read the period on each invoice. Amounts and lines are correct.

## Status
Fix planned for the Console release in May 2027.

##### customer-success-and-support/support-process/partner-mdf-credit-requests-2027.json
title: Partner Program: Market Development Fund (MDF) Requests
status: published
last_updated: 2027-02-02
body: ## Purpose
Resellers and SI partners sometimes write to Support asking for "credits" for joint marketing. Those are Market Development Funds (MDF), not billing credits.

## What Support does
- MDF requests are handled by Partnerships in the partner portal. Point the partner there; don't open a billing case.
- MDF is paid against approved campaign invoices from the partner. It never appears as a credit on a Redwood invoice and has no effect on the partner's usage bill.
- Partnerships approves MDF up to $5,000 per partner per quarter; larger requests go to the partner agreement owner.

## Not MDF
A partner asking about a charge on their own Redwood invoice is an ordinary billing question: follow the billing case routing page.

##### customer-success-and-support/support-process/merging-duplicate-support-conversations-2027.json
title: Support Console: Merging Duplicate Conversations
status: published
last_updated: 2027-02-10
body: ## Purpose
Customers often open a second conversation about an issue they already raised, by email and chat at once. This page covers merging those conversations. Duplicate charges on an invoice are a different thing; see the credits and disputes page.

## When to merge
- Same customer, same issue, both conversations open.
- Keep the older conversation and merge the newer one into it.
- Don't merge conversations from different orgs, even if the issue is identical.

## After merging
- Reply once, in the kept conversation, and say the other one was merged.
- A case already opened from either conversation stays as it is; don't open a second case for the same issue.

_Last reviewed 2027-02-10._

description: Summary: The per-request usage writer cannot keep up with Q1 traffic: the Console usage page falls behind by hours during peaks and the backfill job double-writes on retry. Move the writer to hourly batches. Batched usage is complete and exact but appears in the Console up to 60 minutes after the request. Support's missing-usage threshold changes with the cut-over (Dev Patel to update the routing page). Plan: 1) Build the hourly batch writer behind a flag; write to a shadow table and compare totals for two weeks. 2) Freeze the per-request writer and switch the Console usage page to the batch table. 3) Cut over at a month boundary so no invoice period mixes both writers. 4) Remove the per-request writer and the backfill job. Acceptance: Shadow totals match the per-request writer to the token for 14 consecutive days. Every successful request appears on the Console usage page within 60 minutes. No invoice period contains usage from both writers.

description: Summary: The per-request usage writer cannot keep up with Q1 traffic: the Console usage page falls behind by hours during peaks and the backfill job double-writes on retry. Move the writer to hourly batches. Batched usage is complete and exact but appears in the Console up to 60 minutes after the request. Support's missing-usage threshold changes with the cut-over (Dev Patel to update the routing page). Plan: 1) Build the hourly batch writer behind a flag; write to a shadow table and compare totals for two weeks. 2) Freeze the per-request writer and switch the Console usage page to the batch table. 3) Cut over at a month boundary so no invoice period mixes both writers. 4) Remove the per-request writer and the backfill job. Acceptance: Shadow totals match the per-request writer to the token for 14 consecutive days. Every successful request appears on the Console usage page within 60 minutes. No invoice period contains usage from both writers.

body: ## Purpose
The support console can look up a customer's billing account, issue a credit note against invoice lines, and open a billing dispute. This page defines when Support uses each one. It amends the billing routing page for duplicate charges only; everything else on that page still applies. This version is effective from 26 February 2027 and adds how to tell the copy from the original. Support's per-line limit is set in Finance's Billing Adjustments Approval Matrix (Finance shared drive), which FP&A revised in February 2027; check the matrix for the limit that applies to the invoice in front of you.

## Look up the account first
- Look up the customer's billing account in the console before you quote an amount, a plan, an invoice line, or whether a charge is a duplicate. You can find the account by its account id or by the customer's org name; ask for one of them if the customer hasn't given either.
- Quote amounts as the console shows them. Don't restate a figure the customer gives you as fact.

## Duplicate charges: what Support may credit
A charge is a confirmed duplicate only when the console shows two lines on the same direct Redwood invoice that bill the same request IDs. A similar description or the same amount on its own is not enough.

| Situation | What Support does |
|---|---|
| Confirmed duplicate, duplicated line within the limit | Issue one credit note with reason `duplicate` for the full amount of the duplicated line, against that line. No handoff is needed. Tell the customer the amount credited. |
| Confirmed duplicate, duplicated line over the limit | Don't credit. Open a dispute on the duplicated line (reason `duplicate_charge`, with the request IDs) and hand the case to Billing Ops with the invoice number, the line and the dispute id. |
| Duplicate the console doesn't confirm (different request IDs, or no second line) | Don't credit. Collect the intake details and hand the case to Billing Ops as the routing page describes. |

Credit or dispute the copy, not the original. Each request's usage record names the invoice line that bills it; of the two lines, the one no usage record points to is the duplicated line.

The limit is per duplicated line and applies to the line's full amount. Don't split a larger duplicate into several smaller credits.

## What Support never credits
- Goodwill, exceptions, SLA credits, or any credit someone says a manager, sales rep or Redwood engineer already approved. These stay with Finance, per the #support guidance from FP&A. Route the request; don't issue anything from the console.
- Marketplace purchases, which are billed by the marketplace.

## Telling the customer
- Say what you did: the credit note and its amount, or that a dispute is open and Billing Ops has the case. Don't promise the outcome of a dispute or a date.

## Telling the copy from the original
Each request's usage record names the one invoice line that bills it. When two lines bill the same request IDs:
1. Query the usage records for those request IDs.
2. The line their records point to is the original. Leave it alone.
3. The other line is the copy. Credit or dispute only the copy, for its full amount.
If the records point to neither line, or to both, the console doesn't confirm a duplicate: hand the case to Billing Ops as an unconfirmed duplicate.

## What Billing Ops needs in a duplicate handoff
| Field | Where it comes from |
|---|---|
| Invoice number | The console invoice record |
| Both line IDs, original and copy | The console invoice lines |
| Request IDs | The customer, checked against the usage records |
| Window | In the account's billing timezone |
| Dispute id | The dispute you opened, when the line is over the limit |
| What the customer asked for | The conversation |

## After a credit note
- The credit is applied to the next invoice, or to the invoice being issued if it is issued before the close (see Finance's close calendar).
- The customer sees it as a credit line with the original invoice number.
- Don't issue a second credit note for the same line. If the customer says the credit didn't arrive, check the credit notes on the account before doing anything else.

## Common mistakes
- Crediting the original line instead of the copy.
- Crediting a line because two lines share a description or an amount, without matching request IDs.
- Splitting a line over the limit into several credits.
- Crediting a marketplace purchase: the marketplace bills those, so Support has nothing to credit.
- Telling the customer a dispute will succeed, or when Billing Ops will finish.

## Questions
Ask in #support-billing. Page owner: Dev Patel.

content: ## Purpose
This page documents Redwood Inference’s revenue recognition and invoicing implications for AWS Marketplace and Google Cloud Marketplace (GCP Marketplace) transactions, including:
- How we recognize revenue for usage-based and contract-based marketplace purchases
- How marketplace fees (revenue share) are recorded
- How refunds/credits are handled (and what we can/can’t do within each marketplace)
- How to reconcile marketplace reporting to Redwood internal billing/metering

This is an internal Finance + Legal reference intended to be consistent with ASC 606 / IFRS 15 principles. It is not customer-facing.

## Scope
In scope:
- Hosted API (usage-based)
- Dedicated (reserved capacity contracts) when transacted via marketplace (where supported)
- Private (platform fee + support) when transacted via marketplace (typically via private offers)
- Compliance / support add-ons sold as separate dimensions/SKUs

Out of scope:
- Direct (non-marketplace) contracts and invoicing (see standard Order Form + invoicing runbook)
- Technical metering implementation details (see Billing Catalog + Marketplace Metering docs)

## Definitions and key objects
- Marketplace “Seller of Record”: AWS/GCP is the billing party to the end customer; Redwood receives net proceeds.
- Marketplace “Private Offer”: negotiated pricing/terms within marketplace tooling; acceptance and billing occurs through AWS/GCP.
- Entitlement: the marketplace subscription record used to provision/limit Redwood usage.
- Metering dimension: the billable unit reported to AWS/GCP (e.g., tokens, requests, capacity-hours), mapped from Redwood internal meters.
- Net proceeds: amount remitted to Redwood after marketplace revenue share and (where applicable) taxes handled by marketplace.

## Accounting policy overview
### Principal vs agent (gross vs net)
In most marketplace scenarios Redwood is the primary party delivering the service (we host/operate the inference platform) and AWS/GCP facilitates procurement and billing. However, the end customer is billed by the marketplace and the marketplace collects consideration.

Policy position (default):
- We record revenue on a gross basis for the service delivered to the customer, with marketplace revenue share recorded as a selling expense (or contra-revenue only if required by local statutory guidance). 
- We record Accounts Receivable against the marketplace (not the end customer) to the extent a receivable exists based on reports/remittance timing.

If a specific private offer or marketplace program introduces conditions that materially change control indicators (e.g., marketplace controls pricing and has primary responsibility for delivery), Finance must re-assess principal/agent for that program/region.

### Revenue recognition timing by purchase type
1) Usage-based (Hosted API) via marketplace
- Performance obligation: stand-ready access to API + actual usage (tokens/embeddings/reranks).
- Recognition: as usage occurs (typically daily), based on Redwood internal metering as the system of record, reconciled to marketplace metering reports.
- Cutoff: revenue accrued through period-end for delivered usage regardless of when marketplace remits cash.

### General rule
- Refunds/credits to marketplace customers must be processed through the marketplace mechanisms, not through Redwood’s direct invoicing.
- Redwood may provide service credits inside Redwood (e.g., additional usage allowance) only if consistent with:
  - Marketplace policies
  - The customer’s private offer terms
  - Revenue recognition guidance (credits may reduce transaction price)

- Support: when a marketplace customer asks for a refund, a credit, or their invoice, point them to the marketplace's own process and invoice documentation. If they ask for a Redwood-branded invoice, tell them it would need Legal approval, which Redwood doesn't give for marketplace invoices. No Redwood case is needed for any of these; open a Billing Engineering case only for a Redwood vs marketplace metering mismatch.

### Usage-based disputes (Hosted API)
Common scenarios:
- Customer claims unexpected spend due to misconfiguration
- Metering mismatch (Redwood vs marketplace)

Process:
1) Support confirms incident/dispute scope and time window.
2) Billing Engineering validates internal metering and dimension mapping for the subscription entitlement.
3) Finance determines whether an adjustment is warranted.
4) If warranted:
   - Prefer marketplace credit/refund path (AWS/GCP credit memo equivalent), following marketplace seller workflows.
   - If marketplace cannot issue retroactive adjustments for certain dimensions, Legal + Finance decide on an alternative (e.g., issuing a future-period discount via private offer amendment).

Accounting:
- Refunds reduce revenue in the period identified (or as a subsequent event if applicable), with corresponding reduction in receivable from marketplace.

### Subscription cancellations
- Marketplace cancellations generally stop future billing but do not automatically refund past periods.
- For prepaid/annual private offers, refunds depend on private offer terms and marketplace policy.

Accounting:
- If a refund is approved, reverse deferred revenue for the remaining term and reduce receivable/cash accordingly.

### Promotional credits / trials
Policy:
- Avoid marketplace “$0 with credits” structures that are ambiguous for revrec.
- If a marketplace trial is offered:
  - Ensure the trial is clearly separate from paid subscription/usage.
  - Track conversion and start date of paid entitlement.

If Redwood grants credits inside the Redwood platform (non-marketplace):
- Treat as variable consideration / discount, and ensure it is reflected in net revenue where it impacts the transaction price.
- Do not represent internal credits as marketplace credits.

## Reconciliation: marketplace reports vs Redwood internal billing
### Source of truth
- Redwood internal metering is the operational source of truth for usage delivered.
- Marketplace reports are the commercial source of truth for amounts billed/collected.
- Reconciliation is required at least monthly, and weekly during launch/transition periods.

### Minimum reconciliation outputs (monthly close)
For each marketplace (AWS, GCP) and each SKU/dimension:
- Units billed (marketplace) vs units metered (Redwood)
- Gross billed amount (marketplace) vs gross revenue recognized (Redwood)
- Marketplace fees (per statement) vs accrued fees
- Net remittance vs cash received
- Open receivable balance vs “due from marketplace” aging based on remittance schedule

1) Extract Redwood internal usage summary by marketplace entitlement
- Group by: marketplace (AWS/GCP), seller account, entitlement ID, SKU, dimension, day/month

- AWS: metering/billing reports + disbursement/remittance reports
- GCP: marketplace earnings and billing exports (as provided by partner portal)

3) Map dimensions
- Use the approved SKU mapping catalog (v2) as the only mapping reference.
- Any unmapped dimensions or new SKUs must be flagged to Product + Billing (risk of misbilling and incorrect revr

body: ## About this page
The source for the public error reference on the docs site. Every error the Hosted API returns is listed with its HTTP status, its `error.code`, what causes it and what the client should do. Changes here are published to the docs site in the next docs release.

## Error format
Errors return JSON: `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "...", "request_id": "..."}}`. The `request_id` is the attempt identifier shown on the Console usage page.

## Errors
| HTTP status | `error.code` | Cause | What to do |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_request` | Malformed JSON, unknown parameter, or a value out of range | Fix the request; don't retry unchanged |
| 401 | `invalid_api_key` | Missing, revoked or mistyped API key | Check the key in Console > API keys |
| 402 | `quota_exceeded` | A Free workspace used its monthly included amount, or a paid workspace with overage disabled reached its hard limit | Add a payment method or upgrade in Console billing settings; Free requests work again when the next month starts |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | The key's project can't use this model or region | Ask a workspace admin to grant access |
| 404 | `model_not_found` | Unknown or retired model name | Use a model from the models list |
| 409 | `idempotency_conflict` | An `Idempotency-Key` was reused with a different body | Use a new key for a new request |
| 413 | `payload_too_large` | The request exceeds the model's context window or 20 MB | Shorten the input |
| 429 | `rate_limited` | Requests or tokens per minute above the workspace's rate limit, on any plan | Retry after the `Retry-After` header; spread traffic |
| 500 | `internal_error` | An unexpected server error | Retry with backoff; report the `request_id` if it persists |
| 503 | `overloaded` | Temporary capacity shortage in the region | Retry with backoff or use another region |

## Rate limits are not quotas
`429 rate_limited` is about speed: too many requests or tokens in a minute. It clears within a minute. A quota is about volume over a month and is reported with its own status above. Don't tell a customer to wait a minute for a quota error, or to upgrade for a rate limit unless they need a higher rate.

## Retries
Retry 429, 500 and 503 with exponential backoff and jitter. Don't retry 4xx errors other than 429 without changing the request. Each retried attempt that the gateway admits is a separate request with its own `request_id`.

## Changes
| Date | Change |
|---|---|
| 2027-02-10 | Added `idempotency_conflict` |
| 2026-11-02 | Page created from the docs-site error table; Free-tier monthly limits listed under their own status instead of `429` |
=====PACKAGES

I've updated the agent for R1. All five R1 practice conversations went correctly (one after a fix), and the offline tests pass from a read-only copy under the sandbox limits.

**What changed in `/app/R`**
3,561 records were added and 3 core policy pages were revised in place: the Finance approval matrix, the case routing page, and the payment-failures page. Most additions are noise; about 40 are real 2027 policy pages. Below is where I settled on authority:

- **Credit limit:** Finance's matrix now allows $250 per duplicated line for invoices rated on the 2027 price book and $500 for earlier ones. The Finance close calendar says the 2027 price book applies to usage from March 2027. The drafts (a $1,000 refund authority, a pilot for crediting contract accounts, a 2-hour missing-usage threshold, the price-book rollout plan) don't change anything.
- **Support Charter 2027:** Support may credit only self-serve accounts. A duplicate on a contract or enterprise account gets a dispute and a Billing Ops case. I also enforced this in `issue_credit_note`, because it's a hard authority rule.
- **Credits and disputes page v2:** the copy is the line no usage record points to, not the later line. `get_invoice` now works this out from the usage records.
- **Confirm before you write:** a credit or dispute needs an explicit yes; a plain handoff needs no confirmation. If the developer says no, the agent writes nothing, not even a case. The hooks enforce this.
- **Payment-processor incidents:** a failure inside a published incident window gets no case.
- **Card data:** card numbers in any form are covered, including spelled-out digits and the last four. Card changes are now done by the customer in Console billing settings, with no case.
- **Credit balances:** from 1 April 2027, balances come only from the new credit ledger. A Finance meeting decided the old `credit_grants` table is frozen. Balances are now computed from the ledger.
- **Other new rules:** the missing-usage threshold is 60 minutes for requests after the hourly-batch cut-over (2027-03-01 00:00 UTC). A Free plan over its monthly limit now gets 402, not 429. For marketplace customers, Support points them to the marketplace's own process; the only case allowed is to Billing Engineering for a metering mismatch.
- **Superseded pages:** I flagged the v1 credits page, the 2025 free-tier page and the 2026 dunning schedule as replaced. They stay searchable for history but rank below their replacements.

**Console format change (April 2027)**
- Money fields are now `{"value", "currency"}` objects.
- The writable tables use `billing_account_id`.
- Escalated cases need a `priority`; the agent sets `normal`, per the #support announcement the record-format page points to.
- The tools now read field names from the live `describe()`.

**Other changes**
- The index was rebuilt with the 2027 policy pages added: 1,174 records with vectors (8,609 chunks) and 5,921 searchable by text only. The embedding cache meant only the new chunks were embedded.
- There is a new `payments-and-credits` skill, and the other two skills were updated.
- There is a new `date_calculator` tool.

**Practice results**

| Case | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Contract-account $60 duplicate | No credit; dispute on the copy line, then a Billing Ops case |
| Failed payment inside the 2027-04-06 incident window, with a spelled-out card number (my script) | No case; card number redacted; customer told to change the card in Console. Fix needed (below) |
| Ledger balance | $120.00 left, expiring 2027-04-10 |
| Free plan 402 | Correct, citing the 2027 error reference over the old 429 page |
| R0 $180 duplicate (regression) | Credit written in the new money format, on the copy line, under the $500 limit |

The fix: the newest incident notice gives no retry-completion date. In the payment run the agent first answered correctly (Monday 2027-04-12, three business days after the window per past notices). On the follow-up it "corrected" itself to Friday 2027-04-10 by counting calendar days. I added `date_calculator` and told the skill to compare all past notices in business days. That fix is tested offline only, since no practice runs remain.

Not re-run live in R1: the look-alike duplicate, the SLA contract case, and the marketplace cases. Their code paths are covered offline.

`build/README.md` has the R1 change log. I updated the memory note, and the build script saves an R1 source inventory with each full rebuild for any later release.
